title: Tenali Raman and the Cure for the King's Cold

keywords: the cure for the king's cold
full_text:
King Krishnadevaraya was struck by a severe head cold and throat congestion. He lay in his royal bedchamber, wrapped in heavy woolen shawls, his nose red, his eyes watering, coughing and grumbling in foul humor.
The royal physicians prepared bitter herbal decoctions of black pepper, neem, and ginger, but the King spat them out, refusing to drink the foul-tasting draughts, shouting at his ministers and threatening to banish his doctors.

The royal household walked on tiptoe, terrified of provoking the irritable monarch.
Tenali Raman entered the bedchamber carrying no medicine bowls or herbs, but wearing an absurd, oversized turban made of a braided straw floor mat, balanced precariously with a giant yellow pumpkin tied to its peak!

The King blinked his watery eyes, glared at Tenali, and croaked:
'Tenali! What is that ridiculous monstrosity on your head? Have you come to mock your suffering Emperor?'

Tenali bowed with exaggerated solemnity, wobbling the heavy pumpkin:
'Maharaj! I have consulted the greatest veterinarian of the royal elephant stables! He assured me that your cold was caused by an excess of heavy thoughts weighing down your royal head.
To balance the cosmic humors, I have worn this pumpkin hat, and I have brought the imperial royal decree of elephant etiquette!'

Tenali pulled out an enormous palm leaf and began reading fabricated royal rules in an absurd, nasal, high-pitched voice:
'Rule Number One: Any elephant that sneezes in the presence of the King must bow thrice, wipe its trunk with a silk handkerchief measuring forty cubits, and recite a poem in praise of mangoes!
Rule Number Two: Any physician who prepares bitter neem soup must first drink three buckets of his own potion in the public square while balancing a goose on his forehead!'

The mental image of the dignified court physicians balancing geese while drinking buckets of neem soup was so overwhelmingly hilarious that King Krishnadevaraya could no longer contain himself.
A snort escaped his nose, followed by a chuckle, and then the Emperor burst into roaring, body-shaking, tearful laughter:
'Ha-ha-ha! Ho-ho-ho! Stop, Tenali, stop! My ribs are aching!'

As the King laughed uproariously, his chest opened, he sneezed three tremendous sneezes that cleared his blocked nasal passages completely, and his heavy headache vanished!
He wiped his eyes, breathed deeply without coughing, and realized with astonishment that his throat was clear and his fever was broken!

The King sat up in bed, energized and refreshed:
'Tenali, your absurd pumpkin hat and witty prescription have done what forty bowls of bitter medicine could not! Laughter is indeed the sovereign remedy of nature!'
The King rewarded Tenali with a basket of sweet apples, proving that joy and humor possess genuine healing power.
moral: Hearty laughter and joyful spirits are the most potent medicine for both bodily ailments and mental gloom.
